title: Heat-health action plan activation and emergency department visits: evidence for the board
subtitle: Narrative review before the 2027 heat season
statement: The regional heat-health action plan activated on 7 days last summer, while emergency departments reported heat-related visits on at least 15 other days. The board asks whether lowering the activation threshold would reduce emergency department visits and ambulance calls, who would benefit, and what activation costs. The evidence is mostly time-series studies and grey reports, and the board needs a clear account of what is known and how certain it is.
whoAffected: About 700,000 residents, especially older people living alone, low-income neighbourhoods and people without cars; emergency departments; the health unit's outreach and cooling centre staff; the board.
whatHurts: Heat illness and emergency visits on days below the threshold; alert fatigue and cost if activation is too frequent; unequal benefit if alerts reach those least at risk.
currentPractice: Activation at two days above 31 degrees with night-time lows above 20: public alerts, cooling centres, outreach calls to about 4,000 registered residents and hospital preparation.
whyNow: The board wants an answer before the 2027 heat season.
patientCenteredGoal: Residents most at risk of heat illness are reached in time and stay out of emergency departments.
summary: Problem framed for a narrative review of activation, thresholds, equity and cost.
